exposure: Mode of delivery in the first birth (emergency caesarean section, planned caesarean section, instrumental vaginal birth, spontaneous vaginal birth)
cohort: 94,451 neonates born in Sweden between 1999 and 2015 as a second child to a mother who had her first birth by caesarean section
finding: Spontaneous vaginal birth after a previous caesarean section was associated with better neonatal outcomes overall within 28 days after birth compared with other modes of birth.
mod_finding: Compared to spontaneous vaginal birth, emergency caesarean section and instrumental vaginal birth were associated with increased risks of neonatal infection, asphyxia/respiratory distress, hospital care, and mortality, while planned caesarean section was associated with a decreased risk of neonatal infection.
